literal_source_claim: A positive solution of the Kadison-Singer problem.
canonical_claim: For d,m,r in Nat with 0 < r, delta in Real with 0 <= delta, and u : Fin m -> C^d, if sum_i u_i u_i* = I and norm(u_i)^2 <= delta for every i, then the indices admit an r-part labeled partition whose every part has rank-one sum operator norm at most (1/sqrt(r) + sqrt(delta))^2.
domain_and_universes: d,m,r : Nat; delta : Real; u : Fin m -> EuclideanSpace C (Fin d). The root is finite dimensional over C; no free universes.
quantifiers: forall u : Fin m -> EuclideanSpace C (Fin d)
exists color : Fin m -> Fin r
hypotheses: sum_i rankOne C (u i) (u i) = ContinuousLinearMap.id C (EuclideanSpace C (Fin d))
conclusion: For each j, the operator norm of the sum of rank-one operators over the fiber color i = j is at most (1 / sqrt(r) + sqrt(delta))^2.
excluded_degenerate_cases: Only r = 0 and delta < 0 are excluded. d = 0, m = 0, and empty labeled parts remain allowed; the identity-sum hypothesis controls feasibility.
